# Real Numbers — Formula Sheet



## Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic

**Prime Factorisation Form**


Every composite number $x$ can be uniquely expressed (factorised) as a product of powers of primes:


$$x = p_1^{k_1} \cdot p_2^{k_2} \cdots p_n^{k_n}$$


Where:

* $p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_n$ are distinct prime numbers


* $k_1, k_2, \dots, k_n$ are positive integers



---

**HCF and LCM (Prime Factorisation Method)**

* **$\text{HCF}(a, b)$:** Product of the smallest power of each common prime factor involved in the numbers.


* **$\text{LCM}(a, b)$:** Product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.



---

**HCF and LCM Relationship for Two Numbers**


For any two positive integers $a$ and $b$:


$$\text{HCF}(a, b) \times \text{LCM}(a, b) = a \times b$$

Equivalent forms:


$$\text{LCM}(a, b) = \frac{a \times b}{\text{HCF}(a, b)}$$

$$\text{HCF}(a, b) = \frac{a \times b}{\text{LCM}(a, b)}$$

> Warning: $\text{HCF}(p, q, r) \times \text{LCM}(p, q, r) \ne p \times q \times r$ for three numbers.
> 
> 

---

**HCF and LCM Formulas for Three Numbers**


For any three positive integers $p$, $q$, and $r$:

$$\text{LCM}(p, q, r) = \frac{p \cdot q \cdot r \cdot \text{HCF}(p, q, r)}{\text{HCF}(p, q) \cdot \text{HCF}(q, r) \cdot \text{HCF}(p, r)}$$

$$\text{HCF}(p, q, r) = \frac{p \cdot q \cdot r \cdot \text{LCM}(p, q, r)}{\text{LCM}(p, q) \cdot \text{LCM}(q, r) \cdot \text{LCM}(p, r)}$$

---

## Irrational Numbers & Divisibility Properties

**Prime Divisibility Property**


Let $p$ be a prime number and $a$ be a positive integer:


$$\text{If } p \text{ divides } a^2, \text{ then } p \text{ divides } a$$

---

**Irrationality Criterion**


For any prime number $p$:


$$\sqrt{p} \text{ is irrational}$$

*(e.g., $\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{3}$, $\sqrt{5}$ are irrational)*

---

**Properties of Rational and Irrational Operations**

* $\text{Rational} \pm \text{Irrational} = \text{Irrational}$

* $\text{Non-zero Rational} \times \text{Irrational} = \text{Irrational}$

* $\dfrac{\text{Non-zero Rational}}{\text{Irrational}} = \text{Irrational} \quad \text{and} \quad \dfrac{\text{Irrational}}{\text{Non-zero Rational}} = \text{Irrational}$
